headline: Toledo Fire & Rescue Deputy Chief Daniel Brown-Martinez placed on paid leave after two substantiated sexual harassment investigations
paragraphs: The Toledo Fire & Rescue Department placed Deputy Chief Daniel Brown-Martinez on paid administrative leave as of early November 2026, the 13abc I-TEAM reported November 5 and The Blade confirmed November 6. Brown-Martinez holds the rank of deputy chief over Training, EAP, Communications, Recruitment, Public Education, and the Community Engagement Bureau — a wide administrative portfolio at the department. A disciplinary hearing was underway as of the November 5 report, with testimony continuing the following week. The department told 13abc it would not discuss specifics of the investigation or the pending disciplinary process; the Toledo Firefighters union had not publicly responded to requests for comment.

Two separate internal investigations were substantiated against Brown-Martinez. A September 2026 investigation found sufficient evidence to support allegations of repeated sexual comments and jokes in the workplace, as well as physical contact at a meeting in October 2025. A second probe, related to a June 2026 incident at department headquarters, also substantiated allegations of sexually explicit remarks made in front of co-workers. The department has faced a pattern of discrimination and harassment complaints stretching across multiple years, including a 2019 Ohio Civil Rights Commission finding of probable cause in a gender-discrimination complaint involving the department's first female assistant chief.
why_it_matters: Toledo Fire & Rescue is one of the departments at the center of the post-Issue 16 budget debate, with roughly half of the 73 worst-case layoffs targeted at police and fire. A substantiated leadership accountability action at the department during this fiscal pressure window — with the 2027 budget due November 15 — adds institutional stress at the same time city leaders are navigating potential staffing reductions. The department has a documented pattern of harassment and discrimination complaints; whether this case produces lasting disciplinary action or structural reform will be a signal about the department's accountability culture entering a period of potential significant workforce contraction.
